about.title: About The School District of Osceola County
about.content: The School District of Osceola County, Florida is the countywide public school system for Osceola County. Its calendar is used by families in Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Poinciana, Celebration, Buenaventura Lakes, Harmony, Narcoossee, and other communities along the southern and eastern side of the Orlando metro area. The district calendar lists teacher preplanning, first and last student days, grading periods, progress report and report card dates, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Winter Break, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Rodeo Day, Spring Break, Memorial Day, teacher workdays, professional learning days, and emergency make-up day notes.

about.title: Why Osceola Calendar Planning Is Different
about.content: Osceola County sits between Orlando's tourism economy, Lake Nona-area growth, the Florida Turnpike, and large residential communities such as Poinciana and St. Cloud. Many families coordinate school breaks with theme-park, hotel, restaurant, healthcare, logistics, and shift-based work schedules. The district also serves communities with long commutes across US-192, the Turnpike, Narcoossee Road, and I-4. Because hurricane season overlaps with the first semester, the official calendar's emergency make-up day language is not a footnote: it can change whether a teacher workday remains a student holiday.

planningTips.title: Osceola Calendar Reminders

Recheck official Osceola updates before booking childcare or travel around teacher workdays and major breaks.

customSections.label: Local Calendar Factors for Osceola Families
customSections.content: Osceola families often search by community, but the main student calendar is published districtwide by The School District of Osceola County. The local factors that most affect calendar planning are not extra holidays; they are work schedules, commute corridors, emergency make-up days, and program-specific calendars.

groups.label: Communities using the district calendar
items: Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Poinciana, Celebration, Buenaventura Lakes, Harmony, Narcoossee, and other Osceola County communities use the districtwide student calendar for main academic dates.
Campus-level orientation, testing, athletics, graduation, and program schedules can still differ from the districtwide academic calendar.

groups.label: Local calendar factors
items: Rodeo Day is a local February student holiday that families new to Osceola may not expect.
Tourism, hospitality, restaurant, healthcare, logistics, and shift-based work schedules can make Thanksgiving, Winter Break, Spring Break, Rodeo Day, and teacher workdays harder to cover.
US-192, the Florida Turnpike, Narcoossee Road, and I-4 commute corridors can make single-day student holidays important for pickup and childcare planning.
Emergency make-up day language matters during hurricane season because a listed teacher workday can become a student attendance day if needed.

customSections.label: Osceola Planning Notes for Families
customSections.content: Osceola's school calendar has several planning details that are easy to miss in the PDF. This section focuses on how official calendar labels affect family decisions after the dates are already known.

groups.label: Decision points
items: Rodeo Day requires separate childcare or work coverage because many workplaces do not observe it.
Teacher workdays after grading periods should be checked again if emergency make-up time becomes necessary.
No early-release Wednesday exceptions can change normal pickup routines even when school remains in session.

groups.label: When to verify with the school
items: Verify campus communications for testing, athletics, graduation, orientation, and program events.
Check school-level messages before assuming districtwide dates cover PATHS or other specialized schedules.
Use district announcements as the final source for emergency make-up decisions.

customSections.label: About The School District of Osceola County
customSections.content: The School District of Osceola County, Florida is the countywide public school system for Osceola County. Families in Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Poinciana, Celebration, Buenaventura Lakes, Harmony, Narcoossee, and nearby communities generally use the districtwide calendar for main academic dates, while campus-level events, testing, athletics, graduation, and program schedules may differ.

groups.label: Why calendar planning differs locally
items: Osceola sits inside the Orlando-Kissimmee-Sanford metro area, where tourism, shift work, and cross-county commutes can make single-day student holidays more disruptive.
The official calendar includes Rodeo Day, emergency make-up day notes, grading periods, teacher workdays, professional learning days, and no early-release Wednesday exceptions.
Families should use the official district calendar as the source of record and verify school-specific dates with individual campuses when events fall outside the districtwide academic calendar.

districtFaqs.q: What school district serves Kissimmee, Florida?
districtFaqs.a: Kissimmee public schools are served by The School District of Osceola County, Florida. The districtwide calendar applies to Kissimmee schools unless a specific program or campus publishes a separate schedule.

districtFaqs.q: Does the Osceola school calendar apply to St. Cloud and Poinciana?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. St. Cloud and Osceola County portions of Poinciana are served by The School District of Osceola County. Families should still confirm individual campus events, testing, athletics, and graduation details with their school.

districtFaqs.q: What is Rodeo Day on the Osceola school calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Rodeo Day is a local February student holiday listed on the Osceola school calendar. It is not a federal holiday, so families new to the district should add it separately for childcare and work planning.

districtFaqs.q: How does Osceola handle emergency make-up days?
districtFaqs.a: The official calendars identify some teacher workdays as possible emergency make-up days. If additional make-up days are required beyond those listed, the district says they will be assigned based on the circumstances at the time.

districtFaqs.q: Does PATHS follow the same Osceola calendar?
districtFaqs.a: PATHS may follow a program-specific calendar instead of the districtwide student calendar. PATHS families should verify current-year dates directly with the school or district before making attendance, childcare, or transportation plans.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families verify Osceola calendar changes?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official Osceola Schools calendar page and campus announcements for final confirmation. MySchoolDates summarizes district documents and is not affiliated with The School District of Osceola County.
